question: India's foreign-exchange reserves touched a record high in the week reported in mid-September 2026, making India the fourth-largest holder of forex reserves globally. Which country did India displace from that fourth position, and which three sit above it?

options.text: Displaced Saudi Arabia; above it are China, Japan and the United States
Displaced Russia; above it are China, Japan and Switzerland
Displaced Switzerland; above it are China, the USA and Japan
Displaced Taiwan; above it are China, Japan and Russia

explanation: India's reserves hit a record ~$785.7 billion, overtaking Russia to become the world's 4th-largest holder, behind China, Japan and Switzerland.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India's Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation rose to 9.92% in August 2026. Which major group recorded the *highest* group-level inflation, and roughly at what rate?

options.text: Primary Articles — about 7.8%
Manufactured Products — about 8.4%
Fuel & Power — about 22.9%
Food Index — about 7.1%

explanation: WPI inflation was 9.92% in August 2026; Fuel & Power led at 22.93% (Primary Articles ~7.76%, Manufactured Products ~8.37%).
subject: Current Affairs

question: The Union Cabinet raised the EPFO wage ceiling for mandatory coverage in September 2026. What was the change?

options.text: From Rs 15,000 to Rs 21,000 per month, the first revision in eight years
From Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, the first revision in twelve years
From Rs 21,000 to Rs 30,000 per month, the first revision in five years
From Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000 per month, the first revision since 2001

explanation: The wage ceiling rose from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000/month — the first revision in twelve years — effective 17 September 2026, extending coverage to ~51 lakh more workers.
subject: Current Affairs

question: Regarding the NPCI's revised UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework announced this week, consider the following:
statements: An MDR of 0.4% will apply on Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions above Rs 2,000.
The MDR is capped at Rs 300 per transaction.
Person-to-Person (P2P) transfers and P2M payments up to Rs 2,000 remain outside MDR.

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: All three are correct: 0.4% MDR on P2M above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300, with P2P and sub-Rs 2,000 P2M staying zero-MDR; the framework takes effect 15 October 2026.
subject: Current Affairs

question: The World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026 was held this week. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It was hosted in Mumbai and was the first edition ever held in Asia
It was hosted in Gandhinagar and was its first edition in South Asia
It was hosted in New Delhi as part of the BRICS Summit agenda
It was hosted in Bengaluru and was its 5th global edition

explanation: WCEF 2026 was held in Gandhinagar — its first edition in South Asia (10th edition overall).
subject: Current Affairs

question: 'Operation Deep Manifest', in the news this week, was an enforcement action by which agency, and against what?

options.text: The NIA, against a terror-financing network in the Northeast
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), against Pakistan-origin dry dates transshipped through a third country
The Enforcement Directorate, against a hawala racket routed through Dubai
Customs, against gold smuggling through Kerala ports

explanation: 'Operation Deep Manifest' was a DRI action seizing 362+ MT of Pakistan-origin dry dates transshipped through a third country (UAE/Jebel Ali) to evade origin rules.
subject: Current Affairs

question: *Schizopygopsis waddellii*, reported this week, was recorded in India for the first time. What is it, and where?

options.text: A snow leopard sub-population, in Ladakh
A Tibetan snowtrout (a fish), in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh
A high-altitude orchid, in Sikkim
A migratory crane, in the Rann of Kutch

explanation: *Schizopygopsis waddellii* is a Tibetan snowtrout (fish), recorded in India for the first time in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh.
subject: Current Affairs

question: At the 18th BRICS Summit hosted by India this week, a decision was taken to set up an Expert Working Group on Traditional Medicine. Under which Indian ministry does this initiative primarily sit?

options.text: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
Ministry of Ayush
Ministry of Science & Technology
Ministry of Culture

explanation: The BRICS Traditional Medicine Expert Working Group sits primarily under the Ministry of Ayush.
subject: Current Affairs

question: India and MERCOSUR signed an instrument this week to deepen their trade relationship. What was signed?

options.text: A full Free Trade Agreement replacing the 2004 PTA
The First Additional Protocol to their Preferential Trade Agreement, giving electronic Certificates of Origin legal parity with paper
A Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
A customs union treaty eliminating all tariffs

explanation: India–MERCOSUR signed the First Additional Protocol to their 2004 PTA, giving electronic Certificates of Origin legal parity with paper — not a full FTA.
subject: Current Affairs

question: SEMICON India 2026 was inaugurated this week. Consider:
statements: Its theme was "Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem".
It was held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
It was accompanied by a backgrounder on the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS).

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: All three: theme "Silicon to Systems", venue Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, with an ECMS backgrounder (106 projects, ~Rs 69,548 crore approved investment).
subject: Current Affairs

question: This week India made its first-ever soil-carbon payments to farmers via Direct Benefit Transfer. Which best describes it?

options.text: Rs 2.9 crore transferred to about 2,550 smallholder farmers in Punjab and Haryana
Rs 29 crore transferred to farmers across all Indian states
Rs 2.9 crore transferred to tea growers in Assam
Rs 290 crore transferred under PM-KISAN top-up

explanation: India's first soil-carbon payments: Rs 2.9 crore via DBT to ~2,550 smallholder farmers in Punjab and Haryana.
subject: Current Affairs

question: As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Monthly Bulletin for August 2026, which statement is correct?

options.text: The overall unemployment rate rose to 8.0% and LFPR fell below 50%
The unemployment rate was around 5.0%, with rural unemployment easing and overall LFPR rising to about 55.6%
Urban unemployment crossed 12% for the first time
Female labour-force participation fell sharply during the month

explanation: August 2026 PLFS: unemployment ~5.0%, rural joblessness at a multi-month low (~4.1%), and overall LFPR rising to ~55.6%. Part B — Environment
subject: Current Affairs

question: With reference to the Ramsar Convention, consider the following:
statements: It is an intergovernmental treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
A "Montreux Record" lists Ramsar sites where ecological character has changed or is likely to change.
India has more Ramsar sites than any other country in the world.

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: 1 and 2 are correct. The Ramsar Convention protects wetlands, and the Montreux Record flags sites with adverse ecological change. Statement 3 is wrong — the UK has the most Ramsar sites; India leads in Asia but not the world.
subject: Environment

question: In a biosphere reserve, which zone is legally protected, kept free of human activity, and used only for non-manipulative research and monitoring?

options.text: Buffer zone
Transition zone
Core zone
Manipulative zone

explanation: The core zone is legally protected, undisturbed, and reserved for non-manipulative research; the buffer allows limited activity and the transition zone permits sustainable human use.
subject: Environment

question: The Montreal Protocol and its Kigali Amendment are associated with which environmental objective?

options.text: Reducing greenhouse-gas emissions from aviation
Phasing out ozone-depleting substances, with Kigali adding the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
Regulating trade in endangered species
Controlling transboundary movement of hazardous wastes

explanation: The Montreal Protocol phases out ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment (2016) adds the phase-down of HFCs, which are potent greenhouse gases.
subject: Environment

question: With reference to CITES, consider the following:
statements: It regulates international trade in specimens of wild fauna and flora.
Species listed in Appendix I are the most endangered and international commercial trade in them is generally prohibited.
It is a legally binding convention administered under UNEP.

options.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3

explanation: All three are correct. CITES regulates wildlife trade, Appendix I species get the strictest protection (commercial trade generally banned), and it operates under UNEP.
subject: Environment

question: A keystone species is best defined as one that:

options.text: Is the most numerically abundant species in an ecosystem
Has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance
Is found only within a single geographic region
Occupies the highest trophic level in a food web

explanation: A keystone species has an outsized effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance (e.g., a top predator or a fig tree); removing it can collapse community structure.
subject: Environment

question: Which of the following statements about India's biodiversity hotspots is correct?

options.text: India has four of the world's biodiversity hotspots: the Himalaya, the Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, the Indo-Burma region, and the Sundaland (Nicobar Islands)
India has only one biodiversity hotspot, the Western Ghats
The Eastern Ghats are recognised as a global biodiversity hotspot
The Thar Desert is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots

explanation: India has parts of four hotspots: the Himalaya, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
subject: Environment

question: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 as amended, animals granted the highest degree of protection (absolute protection, stiffest penalties) are listed in:

options.text: Schedule III
Schedule II
Schedule I
Schedule V

explanation: Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 confers the highest protection with the harshest penalties. (After the 2022 amendment the Act was restructured to fewer schedules, but Schedule I retains top protection.)
subject: Environment

question: Mangroves are ecologically valued as "blue carbon" ecosystems. Which statement is correct?

options.text: They store little carbon and are climate-neutral
They sequester and store large amounts of carbon in their biomass and waterlogged soils, and buffer coasts against storm surges
They grow only in freshwater lakes
They are exclusively found along India's western coast

explanation: Mangroves store large amounts of "blue carbon" in biomass and waterlogged soils and protect coasts from storm surges and erosion.
subject: Environment
